entities.definition: Grid-like network consisting of pigmented lines and hypopigmented holes.
entities.notes: Level 1 melanocytic criterion. Also seen in dermatofibroma (Table 4 footnote *).

entities.definition: Network with increased variability in the thickness and color of the lines of the network, and increased variability in the size and shape of the holes.
entities.notes: Three-point checklist wording (p446 col 2) differs: 'Irregular or atypical pigment network consisting of thick lines and irregular holes.' No appendix entry exists, so Table 5 is used.

entities.definition: Diffuse pigmentation interrupted by adnexal opening. Usually seen in facial lesions.
Serpiginous interconnecting hypopigmented lines that surround irregularly shaped pigmented structures resembling elongated curvilinear globules.
entities.notes: Table 5 wording is identical. Appears both as a level 1 melanocytic criterion and as a melanoma-specific structure.

entities.definition: More than three clustered, well-demarcated, round to oval, symmetric structures, or three or more of these structures aligned at the lesion's perimeter. May be brown, black, or blue. Diameters are greater than 0.1 mm.
Small, round structures of less than 0.1 mm in diameter. May be black, brown, or blue-gray.
Multiple dots or globules of different size, shape, and color. Asymmetrically or focally distributed within the lesion.
Streaks are radial projections at the periphery of the lesion, extending from the tumor toward the surrounding normal skin; may be brown or black.
entities.notes: Table 5 wording, applying to the melanoma-specific form: 'Radial projections at the periphery of the lesion that are focally and asymmetrically distributed.'

entities.definition: Pseudopods are streaks with finger-like projections with small knobs at the tips.
Radial streaming is streaks without knobs at the tips.
Tiny, blue-gray granules.
entities.notes: Also called granularity. Referred to as 'blue pepper-like granules' in the three-point checklist.

entities.definition: Devoid of dermoscopic structures within the lesion and without manifesting any regression structures. Tend to be tan to light brown, but have lighter pigment compared with the rest of the lesion.
Structureless areas (as above), located at the periphery of the lesion.
entities.notes: Table 5 adds the size threshold the appendix omits: 'Tan areas located at the periphery of the lesion that encompass greater than 10% of the lesion.' Appendix is authoritative for the definition; the 10% threshold is retained from Table 5 because it exists nowhere else.

entities.definition: Dark brown to black homogeneous areas of pigment that obscure visualization of any other structures.
Asymmetrically or focally located at the periphery of the lesion. Irregular blotch will often reveal differing hues.

Include scar-like depigmentation (lighter than the surrounding uninvolved normal skin; appear shiny white under polarized dermoscopy) often combined with peppering; combination of scar-like depigmentation and peppering gives the appearance of a blue-white veil.
entities.notes: Table 5 wording is a shortened form of the same.

entities.definition: Depigmentation lighter than the surrounding uninvolved normal skin; appears shiny white under polarized dermoscopy.
entities.notes: Called 'white scar-like depigmentation' in the three-point checklist.

entities.definition: Confluent blue pigmentation with an overlying white ground-glass haze.
entities.notes: Table 5 entry is 'Blue-white veil overlying raised areas', defined as tending to be asymmetrically located or diffuse throughout the lesion with differing hues. Canonical form for 'blue-whitish veil' and 'blue-white structures'.

entities.definition: Umbrella term covering rosettes, crystalline structures and white shiny areas; more conspicuous with polarized dermoscopy.
entities.source: Appendix p B; Table 4 footnote †, p444

entities.definition: Appear as four white shiny points creating a pattern reminiscent of a four-leaf clover.
Short, white, shiny linear streaks that are often parallel or orthogonal to each other.
entities.notes: Table 5 wording differs: 'White shiny streaks or lines organized orthogonally.' Canonical form for 'white shiny streaks' and 'chrysalis structures'.

entities.definition: Appear as larger structureless areas of shiny white color.
On volar skin (i.e., palms and soles). Parallel rows of pigmentation following the furrows (as seen in nevi) or ridges (as seen in melanoma) of the dermatoglyphics.
Parallel pigment pattern in which the pigmentation follows the furrows of the dermatoglyphics; the nevus polarity.
entities.notes: Name coined here for the benign polarity; the source describes it inside the parallel_pigment_pattern definition rather than naming it.

entities.definition: Parallel pigment pattern in which the pigmentation follows the ridges of the dermatoglyphics; the melanoma polarity.
entities.notes: Name coined here for the malignant polarity; not a named term in the source.

entities.definition: Not defined in the source. Listed as a level 1 melanocytic criterion and illustrated in Figure 2 (5A-5C).
entities.source: Table 4, level 1, p444; Figure 2 caption, p445

entities.definition: Round whitish or yellowish structures that shine brightly (like "stars in the sky") under nonpolarized dermoscopy. Further subclassified as small and starry, and as large and cloudy.
Subclassification of milia-like cysts; the source names the subtype without defining it further.
Subclassification of milia-like cysts; the source names the subtype without defining it further.
Blackhead-like plugs on the surface of the lesion.
Delicate, thin, light brown parallel running lines that do not interconnect to form a grid.
Gyri (ridges or fat fingers) and sulci (fissures) that create a cerebriform surface. These invaginations can be filled with keratin, creating crypts.
Concave invaginations of the lesion border.
Not defined in the source; given only as an additional feature of seborrheic keratosis.

Grid-like pattern that can resemble the pigment network seen in a melanocytic neoplasm. Correspond to interconnecting epidermal ridges on the skin; the holes correspond to comedones or crypts. Lines tend to appear broader compared with the pigment network seen in nevi.
Brown to gray-blue discrete bulbous structures that may coalesce to create a shape that resembles a leaf.
Well-circumscribed brown to gray-blue-brown radial projections meeting at a darker brown central hub.
entities.notes: Canonical form for 'spoke wheel-like structures' and 'concentric structures'.

entities.definition: Variant of spoke wheel-like structures; the source names it as a variant without a separate definition.
entities.source: Table 4, level 2, p444; Figure 4 caption, p448

entities.definition: Large, well-circumscribed ovoid areas; larger than globules.
Multiple, nonaggregated, round, well-circumscribed structures.
entities.notes: Table 4 level 2 wording: 'Multiple blue-gray nonaggregated globules'.

entities.definition: Red (hemangioma), maroon (hemangioma and angiokeratoma), or black (angiokeratoma) lagoons often separated by septae.
entities.notes: Body text p444 col 2 adds blue as a fourth possible color with no lesion assignment.

entities.definition: Not defined in the source; given as an additional BCC feature, qualified as not associated with a history of trauma.
entities.source: Table 4 footnote †, p444; Figure 4 caption, p448

entities.definition: Coiled vessels mimicking the glomerular apparatus of the kidney.
U-shaped vessels. Not infrequently, may be twisted on its axis.
Hairpin vessels on a background with a white halo, common in keratinocytic tumors.
Hairpin vessels on a background with a pink halo or pink background, common in irritated seborrheic keratosis, but can also be seen in cutaneous malignancies.
Vessels with large diameter, branching irregularly into fine capillaries.
entities.notes: Canonical form for 'arborizing blood vessels'.

entities.definition: Branching or nonbranching vessels radiating toward the center of the lesion but without crossing its center. Often associated with white/yellowish popcorn-like globular structures.
Listed as a level 5 vessel morphology in Table 4; the appendix defines only the distribution form (see string_of_pearls_vessels), not a standalone serpiginous vessel morphology.
Vessels distributed in a serpiginous pattern.
entities.notes: Full source name: dotted or glomerular vessels in 'string of pearls' or serpiginous distribution. This is a distribution, not a morphology.

entities.definition: White-yellow follicular openings surrounded by a white halo, over a red background.
Slightly curved vessels.
Red dots (0.01 to 0.02 mm).
Dotted vessels on a milky-red background; associated with Spitz nevi and early melanoma.
Dotted vessels on a tan background; associated with Clark nevi.
Irregular linear/undulating short vessels.
entities.notes: Canonical form for 'serpentine or irregular linear vessels'.

entities.definition: Ill-defined globules of milky-red color and ill-defined areas of milky-red color.
entities.notes: Canonical form for 'milky-red globules/vascular blush'.

entities.definition: Combination of two or more vessel morphologies. Most common combination is dotted and serpentine vessels.
Coiled and tortuous vessels.
Dotted vessels over milky-red backgrounds; serpentine (irregular linear) vessels; polymorphous vessels.
Asymmetry in distribution of dermoscopic color and/or structures in one or two perpendicular axes. The contour or silhouette of the lesion does not factor into whether the lesion is symmetric or not.
entities.notes: Explicitly contrasted with the ABCD mnemonic, which does factor in contour or shape.

entities.definition: The third three-point-checklist criterion: blue-white veil and/or white scar-like depigmentation and/or blue pepper-like granules.
A melanocytic tumor, i.e., melanocytic nevus or melanoma; the melanocytic branch of step 1 of the two-step algorithm.
The nonmelanocytic branch of step 1: dermatofibroma, basal cell carcinoma, seborrheic keratosis, hemangioma.
Benign melanocytic tumor; tends to manifest one of the symmetric patterns depicted in Figure 3.
Named in the source as one of the melanocytic lesion types evaluated in step 2; no dermoscopic definition given.
Benign melanocytic nevus in which any of the ten melanoma-specific structures can also be seen.
entities.source: Table 5 footnote *, p447; Figure 2 caption, p445

entities.definition: Melanocytic nevus showing homogeneous blue pigmentation.
Named in the source as one of the melanocytic lesion types evaluated in step 2; no dermoscopic definition given.
Melanocytic nevus associated with dotted vessels over a tan background.
Melanocytic nevus associated with comma-shaped vessels.
Melanocytic nevus in which arborizing vessels can, on rare occasions, be seen.
Melanocytic nevus associated with comma-shaped and serpentine vessels.
Malignant melanocytic tumor; reveals at least one of the 10 melanoma-specific structures of Table 5.
Melanoma associated with dotted vessels over a milky-red background.
Melanoma associated with milky-red globules and vascular blush.
entities.source: Appendix p E; Figure 1 caption, p442

entities.definition: Melanoma subtype associated with corkscrew vessels.
Melanoma subtype associated with corkscrew vessels.
Metastatic cutaneous melanoma, associated with corkscrew vessels.
Nonmelanocytic malignancy occupying level 2 of the criterion ladder.
Basal cell carcinoma demonstrating pigmented structures including leaf-like structures, spoke wheel-like structures, ovoid nests, and nonaggregated blue-gray globules.
Basal cell carcinoma revealing vascular structures such as arborizing blood vessels.
One of the most common benign epidermal tumors. Clinically characterized by well-circumscribed plaques or papules with pseudohorn cysts, ranging from light brown to dark brown or black.
Seborrheic keratosis showing hairpin vessels on a pink halo or pink background.
Nonmelanocytic lesion characterized by a peripheral delicate pigment network with a central scar-like area.
Nonmelanocytic vascular lesion distinguished dermoscopically by well-demarcated lacunae.
Bright red to violaceous papules that consist of dilated capillaries.
Dark violaceous to black papules that are often keratotic or firm on palpation; distinguished dermoscopically by well-demarcated lacunae.
Lesion associated with the strawberry pattern. The source gives no benign/malignant status and no ladder placement.
Lesion associated with glomerular vessels; named without further definition.
Lesion associated with glomerular vessels; also shows dotted vessels. Named without further definition.
entities.source: Appendix p D; Appendix NOTE, p F

entities.definition: Mimic lesion associated with glomerular vessels and with dotted or glomerular vessels in a string-of-pearls or serpiginous distribution.
entities.notes: Maps to no DermaMNIST class; useful for arguing a lesion away from akiec.

entities.definition: Keratinizing tumor associated with hairpin vessels on a white halo background.
entities.notes: Maps to no DermaMNIST class.

entities.definition: Class of tumors, including keratoacanthoma and seborrheic keratosis, in which hairpin vessels with a white halo background are common.
Mimic lesion associated with crown vessels.
entities.notes: Maps to no DermaMNIST class; useful for arguing a lesion away from bcc.

entities.definition: Mimic lesion associated with crown vessels.
entities.notes: Maps to no DermaMNIST class.

entities.definition: Mimic lesion in which dotted vessels can be seen.
entities.notes: Maps to no DermaMNIST class.

entities.definition: Mimic condition in which polymorphous vessels can be seen.
entities.notes: Maps to no DermaMNIST class.

entities.definition: Class of lesions, along with cysts and furuncles, in which arborizing vessels can also be seen.
entities.notes: Maps to no DermaMNIST class.

entities.definition: A lesion in which no structures or blood vessels are noted; level 7 of the criterion ladder. The source assigns no diagnosis to this level.
DermaMNIST class: actinic keratoses and intraepithelial carcinoma (Bowen's disease).
entities.source: Target label set; source coverage in Appendix pp D-E only

entities.definition: DermaMNIST class: basal cell carcinoma.
entities.source: Target label set; source coverage Table 4 level 2

entities.definition: DermaMNIST class: benign keratosis-like lesions (seborrheic keratosis, solar lentigo, lichen-planus-like keratosis).
entities.source: Target label set; source covers only seborrheic keratosis

entities.definition: DermaMNIST class: dermatofibroma.
entities.source: Target label set; source coverage Table 4 footnote * only

entities.definition: DermaMNIST class: melanoma.
DermaMNIST class: melanocytic nevi.
DermaMNIST class: vascular lesions (angioma, angiokeratoma, pyogenic granuloma, haemorrhage).
entities.source: Target label set; source covers neither pyogenic granuloma nor haemorrhage

entities.definition: Melanocytic lesions. Criteria: pigment network, negative pigment network, aggregated globules, streaks (pseudopods and radial streaming), homogeneous blue pigmentation, pseudonetwork (facial skin), parallel pigment pattern (acral lesions on palms and soles).

Basal cell carcinoma. Criteria: arborizing blood vessels, leaf-like structures, large blue-gray ovoid nests, multiple blue-gray nonaggregated globules, spoke wheel-like structures/concentric structures.
Seborrheic keratosis. Criteria: multiple (three or more) milia-like cysts, comedo-like opening, moth-eaten borders, gyri (ridges) and sulci (fissures), fingerprint-like structures.
Hemangioma/angiokeratoma. Criterion: red, maroon, or black lacunae.
Blood vessels seen in nonmelanocytic tumors. Criteria: arborizing, glomerular, hairpin, crown, and serpiginous vessels.
Blood vessels seen in melanocytic tumors. Criteria: comma-shaped, dotted, serpentine or irregular linear, polymorphous, and corkscrew vessels; milky-red globules/vascular blush.
Structureless lesions. Criterion: no structures or blood vessels noted.

The ordered set of seven levels underlying step 1 of the two-step algorithm, intended to help differentiate melanocytic lesions from dermatofibroma, basal cell carcinoma, seborrheic keratosis and hemangioma.

The foundation for dermoscopic evaluation of skin lesions. Step 1 separates melanocytic from nonmelanocytic lesions; step 2 separates nevi from melanoma within the melanocytic branch, yielding the verdicts nevus, suspect and malignant.
First step: melanocytic vs. nonmelanocytic, evaluated against the seven-level criterion ladder.
Second step: benign vs. malignant melanocytic lesions, applied only to melanocytic lesions, using one of several scoring systems.
Benign melanocytic nevus pattern; name only, no definition in source.
Benign melanocytic nevus pattern; name only, no definition in source.

relations.definition: The subject is a dermoscopic criterion listed at the object level (1-7) of the Table 4 ladder.
Presence of the subject in an image supports the object lesion class. Not a probability statement; the source provides no likelihood scale.
The subject satisfies a criterion belonging to the object level of the Table 4 ladder despite not being a lesion of that level's class.
relations.notes: Used for dermatofibroma, which shows a pigment network but is nonmelanocytic.

relations.definition: Links a lesion entity named in the source to one of the seven DermaMNIST/HAM10000 labels.
The subject is one of the ten structures listed in Table 5. Membership does not imply exclusivity — see the Table 5 footnote on Spitz nevi.
The subject is one of the nine symmetric dermoscopic patterns that melanocytic nevi tend to manifest (Figure 3).
The subject structure was documented in a benign example lesion of the object class.
The subject structure was documented in a malignant example lesion of the object class.
The subject is primarily associated with another entity but is documented as occurring in the object entity too. Carries frequency where the source states one.
The subject separates the two entities in the object list. The discriminating modifier is given in the notes field.
The subject can be mistaken for the object under dermoscopy. Encoded in both directions where the source describes bidirectional confusion.
Links a verdict or lesion class to the id of a compound criterion in the criteria array.
The object is a visible morphological feature of the subject entity.
An explicit exclusion: the object is stated by the source not to be part of the subject's definition.
Attaches a verbatim numeric performance figure to the subject, with metric_type naming what it measures. Used only for the two sensitivity figures in Table 4 footnote †.
The subject is stated to be visible or conspicuous only under the object imaging modality.
relations.notes: Retained on one triple (t_197) because it qualifies a definition. Should not be used as reasoning evidence: HAM10000 mixes polarized and nonpolarized images and the modality is not recoverable from the label.

relations.definition: The subject occurs at the object anatomic site.
The subject usually, but not exclusively, occurs at the object anatomic site.
The subject should prompt consideration of the object as an alternative diagnosis.

Declared in the controlled vocabulary but used in zero triples. Per the extraction spec, histopathologic correlates from the appendix were placed in the notes field of the relevant triple instead of being emitted as their own triples, since they are not visible in an image.
Declared in the controlled vocabulary but unused; confused_with covered every case in this source without ambiguity.
Class membership.
The subject is a narrower kind of the object entity.
The subject is a morphological variant of the object structure, differing by a named modifier.
The subject is a constituent part of the object composite structure or criterion.

vocabulary_notes: No new relations were invented. Two vocabulary relations went unused: histopathologic_correlate (superseded by the notes-field instruction) and mimics (subsumed by confused_with).

combination_logic offers no term for an ordered, top-down evaluated ladder. c_005 (the seven-level ladder) is tagged additive_score for schema conformance only; the ladder is not additive and this tag should be treated as a schema artifact, not a claim about the source.
No probability, likelihood or malignancy-score field appears anywhere. The only two numbers in the graph (t_044, t_045) are sensitivities of a criteria set.
